reviewed_properties: Bytes are counted incrementally before forwarding over-budget chunks or collecting an entire Workbench body. Empty chunks do not grow the Workbench accumulator; malformed UTF-8 is rejected.
One request stream is consumed. The Web Request is created before application entry and preserved through Workbench admission and dispatch; the bounded helper does not clone after authentication.

Public NodeHttpServerRequest.toIncomingMessage and NodeStream.fromReadable with closeOnDone:false separate reader cancellation from premature socket destruction, allowing a complete private 400/413 response.
Abort/disconnect cancellation is wired to the request stream; cancellation does not await an arbitrary producer cancellation promise; listeners and owned reader locks are released.
Host/origin/proxy checks, Microsoft transport sanitization, no-store/nosniff responses and private error messages remain at the existing boundaries.

Workbench and delegated workbench-* paths use at most65536bytes. Other streams use the host MaxBodySize service with finite fallback; exact contract routing preserves the domain25MiB allowance while honoring a lower explicit host budget.

W5 tests preserve incomplete-body complete=false assertions while observing physical socket close/destruction and data/readable listener cleanup. Strict IncomingMessage.destroyed/aborted/close is required for disconnect during an active request, not every answered incomplete request. The Bun raw client waits for remote EOF without sending body EOF.

harness_diagnostics.observed: Bun1.3.14 returned400 with empty bytes for the one-chunk malformed JSON stimulus while the valid65536-byte case succeeded; the job had12 pass and3 fail.
harness_diagnostics.diagnosis: Source-supported client-harness framing issue: Bun defers the first write, and write/end in one tick takes send/startFetch(customBody). The old test imposed Transfer-Encoding:chunked on this non-duplex fast path. Removing the manual header leaves framing to the client and preserves the explicit real-chunked/no-Content-Length assertions in the multi-chunk valid case.
harness_diagnostics.confidence_boundary: No packet capture or runtime reproduction was executed by this reviewer. The matching invalid-input case passed in R3 after the harness correction.

harness_diagnostics.observed: Two tests timed out waiting for IncomingMessage.close after their functional413/upload assertions.
harness_diagnostics.diagnosis: Bun ServerResponse.end detaches the socket and clears socket._httpMessage; NodeHTTPServerSocket close handling finds the request through that field. Therefore response completion can omit the server IncomingMessage.close event in this shim. Revised Bun tests observe response finish/close, reader-listener cleanup and raw-peer EOF for early refusals. The subsequent R4 investigation showed that Node24 also requires a socket-based resource oracle after an early response; strict request destruction remains only for disconnect during active consumption.

The current Node probe uses the real local installation/Node/Effect bridge without importing that graph. It adds no custom loader, mock transport or product rewrite. harness_diagnostics.coverage_limit: This review does not establish that the complete Microsoft graph imports or runs directly under Node24.

harness_diagnostics.observed: Actual job log:14 pass,1 fail,330 expect calls. The sole failure was listener.test.ts line186 expecting complete=false and receiving true after full413 JSON and remote EOF assertions.
harness_diagnostics.diagnosis: For an unconsumed request, Bun ServerResponse.end calls request._dump. That resumes reading with _dumped=true; _read calls emitEOFIncomingMessage, whose next-tick callback sets complete=true without proof that the declared request body arrived.
harness_diagnostics.W4_change: Keep CL65537 with no sent body, remote EOF, full413 JSON, zero readableLength, no application entry/writes, and response/reader cleanup in Bun. Assert complete=false strictly on real Node24 for both chunked excess and excessive declared length. No product change accompanies this correction.

harness_diagnostics.observed: Actual log:1 pass,0 failed assertions,2 tests cancelled at20000ms. The active disconnect/abort test passed. No intermediate stage diagnostics locate the timed-out awaits or establish completed413 assertions in R4.
harness_diagnostics.diagnosis: Node24 resOnFinish removes an answered request from state.incoming before closing the socket. socketOnClose destroys only requests still queued. A partially consumed request is already _consuming and is not dumped; Readable.autoDestroy runs after end, which need not occur for an intentionally incomplete body. NodeStream closeOnDone:false removes its listeners without destroying the IncomingMessage. Thus an unanswered event wait on req.close can hang after the physical resource is already closed.
harness_diagnostics.memory_boundary: freeParser/cleanParser clear parser.socket/incoming/outgoing on socket close. A remaining callback on the request or a non-destroyed request object retained by the test does not by itself establish a live reader/socket leak.
harness_diagnostics.W5_change: Capture the real socket at the request event, await its close with a3000ms discriminating diagnostic, and require socket.destroyed plus data/readable listener counts zero. Keep complete=false for early rejections and strict IncomingMessage.destroyed/aborted/close for disconnect during consumption. Do not raise test deadlines or call product destroy solely to satisfy flags.
harness_diagnostics.confidence_boundary: Diagnosis is supported by pinned Node/Effect sources and the successful R5 result after the test-only oracle correction; no runtime was executed by this reviewer.

additional_claim_limits: Bridge enforcement bounds bytes actually consumed. An arbitrary handler that ignores its body can perform effects before valid EOF; no universal no-write-before-EOF claim is made for every SfInstallation.handler.
A short Content-Length delimits the HTTP message. Tests reject the truncated JSON case; they do not prove detection of every trailing byte or subsequent pipelined message as part of that same body.

The canonical binary-domain fixture proves an authorized upload above65536bytes with exact retained bytes and scanner refusal, not the unintegrated25MiB policy boundary or a live malware-scanner service.
The existing binary application readBytes consumer can retain a closed Web reader lock. Universal WebBody.locked=false is not asserted; this out-of-scope application.ts behavior is not rewritten.
Upstream private implementation symbols were read only to diagnose Bun behavior. Mission74 production code uses public Effect/Node APIs, not those private symbols.

The Node probe destroys its client after response end. Its socket oracle proves physical cleanup after the complete response; it does not alone prove server-initiated closure without client cooperation. The separate Bun raw-wire cases require remote EOF before client destruction.
